title: Playing jazz cadenzas with string quartets and a woodwind quintet
summary: With the Lincoln String Quartet and a woodwind quintet at the Robeson Center music conference he played classical works with jazz cadenzas between movements, 1970-72.

blocks.x: Now, you -- now, here, you have -- could you talk a bit about the work that you were doing with the -- that you did with the string quartets --
Yes, yes.
-- and the harpsicordists and --
Yes.
-- (inaudible).

I've done quite a bit of work with the Lincoln String Quartet of Southern Illinois and the Camarado (PHONETIC) Woodwind Quintet of Western Illinois University and we have done quite a bit of work, especially for the -- sponsored by the National Council on the Arts.
Now, how did this -- how did your involving yourself with those kind of musicians come about?
Yes, well, it so happened that they were invited here to play for an institution called Robeson

Center and so of course, being connected with the Robeson Center here, I had the opportunity to do my bit with them. I was asked to do concerts with them while they were doing a sort of a workshop affair.
It was a music conference.

A music conference. And that's how that started. I had special arrangements written for me and of course, I worked right along with them. You don't usually hear of a bass player playing with a quartet, you know.
Never do, then it's a quintet.

During this happening, I injected my bit of jazz into this department -- of course, normally I played right along with them and of course, in between the different movements, I would play a jazz cadenza, a cadenza leading into the next movement, which might be into a different key even in these pieces that we played and that was quite -- something new that has never been done before.
How did the string quartet react to it?
Oh, my goodness, they really -- Claire, could you tell him about how they reacted?

Well, that was beautiful. He printed that too, when he played with the Indianapolis Symphony. They loved the idea. They took the principals of their orchestra, you know, after he had done his big number with them and they repeated it with the principals of the orchestra and
everyone who's heard it has just flipped over it.
Now, you -- has this been recorded?
No, no.
This hasn't been recorded. Which year did this take place -- which years?
So, three. '70, '71 and '72.
Yeah, right.
